title: To Marsia, Covering Her Eyes with Her Hand
text:
Sending a basket of jasmines to
        a lady

        A jealous portion of your whiteness
is that which today from a green lattice,

        to honor your hand, mine stole,
this one courtly indeed, that one pure.
The
        beautiful dawn among ambers exudes
in its clean cambric a cold substance,

        this one waking earlier than any other day
and its fortune grown greater than
        others.
And
        if you do not know the name of these lush
young ones I offer you
        by the bushel
—who, being so, all look white-haired—

        I will easily believe you can guess it
if among them, Lísida, you mix your
        hands.
If you touch them, you will see they are jasmines.
editorial_note: The translation follows the ornate syntax of the jasmine sonnet while keeping the final tactile reveal.

title: Syria
text:
They said
        in Antiquity that poetry
is a stairway to God. Perhaps it is not
        so
when you read me now. But I knew it the day
that through you I found
        my voice again, dissolved
in a flock of clouds and unruly
goats, which from a crag were stripping the leaves
from the plum tree and
        the cattail, and the thinned faces
of the moon and sun were melting;
the engine was broken and an arrow
of blood on a rock
        marked
the road to Aleppo.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Syrian landscape, the damaged engine, and the blood arrow as the route back to voice.

title: One Year
text:
I return here to tell myself my life
another autumn afternoon
old with
        thirty-three turns around the sun.
I return to fold back into this chair

        feeling its innocence of wood
now that the year makes its thunder

        and shakes me hard, from the root.
On the terrace I begin another descent
to
        hell, to winter.
The leaves of the trees bleed in me.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Montejo's autumn birthday reckoning and the descent from terrace into winter.
